text:
Jessica (Support): @channel FYI we got an escalation from Elliot at Acme — their app is seeing a spike of 500s when they hit our generate endpoint during burst traffic. They expect 429s for rate limit but are getting 5xx. Customer is losing production traffic.

Elliot (Customer): we're seeing ~20% of requests return 502/503 intermittently for minutes at a time, around quota bursts. curl output: ```
$ curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer XXX' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
{"error":"upstream error"}
```
This used to return 429 on heavy traffic. What changed?

Tyler (API): thanks Elliot, forwarding to infra. Jessica can you paste customer headers and request IDs?

Jessica (Support): request-ids: [rQ-20260301-az1-7f2, rQ-20260301-az1-7f3]. They say it started ~2026-03-01 10:12 UTC. No change on their side.

Maria (SRE): quick summary from initial traces: majority of 5xx are originating at the gateway layer when invoking the quota/rate-limiter service. Instead of returning a 429 from the quota service we see a 502/504 bubbled up. Looks like the quota service call is timing out to an internal dependency (redis or quota-orchestrator).

SRE Bot: alert: quota-service latency spike in us-east-1 at 2026-03-01T10:11:30Z — 95th latency 3.4s, >= timeout 2s. Error ratio 8% 5xx.

Tyler (API): that matches customer window. Did we flip any routing for quota-service recently? Kevin?

Kevin (Platform): we pushed a routing change to route internal quota calls to the v2 cluster (better metrics) at 10:05 UTC for a canary. Canary target was 5% traffic. Initial rollout looked fine in canary but at 10:11 we saw a backend flake on v2 that caused timeouts. The fallback should have routed to v1 which returns 429 on limit breaches but it didn't — looks like the timeout path threw 502 instead.

Maria (SRE): reproduction steps I used: 
1) run a small script to open N concurrent connections to /v1/generate with rapid bursts using the customer's API key. 
2) observe gateway logs: ```
[10:11:12] gw: req=rQ-20260301-az1-7f2 -> quota-service: call timeout after 2s
[10:11:12] gw: upstream returned 504, returning 502 to client
```
Notice gateway interpreted dependency timeout as upstream 5xx instead of mapping to 429.

Tyler (API): gateway should never surface 5xx for quota failures. Expectation: if quota-service returns exceed (4xx) -> 429 to client; if quota-service times out because of rate evaluation we should default to safe-deny with 429 (or a configured degraded-mode). Sounds like misroute + missing timeout-to-429 mapping.

Jessica (Support): customer wants ETA and a workaround. They can throttle from their side but they'd rather not.

Maria (SRE): immediate mitigation options: 
- Rollback routing canary (Kevin) to send traffic back to v1 where behavior is stable. 
- Patch gateway to translate quota-service timeouts/dependency errors into 429 for requests whose quota check failed. 
- Short-term: raise quota-service timeout threshold to avoid transient timeouts (risk masking real issues).

Kevin (Platform): rolling back canary now. Executing: `kubectl patch svc/quota-routing -n infra -p '{"spec":{"canaryPercent":0}}'` -> starting at 10:23 UTC. I'll monitor.

SRE Bot: deployment event: quota-routing canary revert started by Kevin at 2026-03-01T10:23:12Z.

Maria (SRE): after rollback, early indicators: 5xx rate dropped from 8% -> 0.6% in the next 3 minutes. Still seeing a handful of 502s attributed to lingering inflight calls.

Tyler (API): good. We need a durable fix: gateway should map quota-service failure modes to client-facing 4xx where appropriate. There's no reason customer's app should see 502 for a rate check failing. Can we open a ticket?

Maria (SRE): filing infra ticket: INFRA-3245 with root-cause hypotheses: v2 quota backend had an internal dependency timeout (redis connection saturation) -> quota-service returned error or timed out -> gateway did not map timeout to 429 -> client observed 5xx. Attach traces and sample request-ids.

Anita (Billing): FYI some customers will open billing disputes if they think we mis-billed due to 5xx. Jessica please note which customers are affected.

Jessica (Support): noted. Elliot I'm escalating your case to enterprise ops. We'll provide mitigation window and credit if warranted. ETA for root fix?

Tyler (API): engineering plan: 
- short term (today): revert canary (done), monitor for 30m, notify affected customers, and add a gateway rule to map quota timeouts -> 429 as a hotfix (non-invasive route).
- medium term (1-2 days): fix quota-service dependency scaling (redis pool/connection settings) and add better health checks for canary backends.
- long term: add explicit SLO for quota-service latency and a contract that gateway should treat quota check failures as soft-deny.

Maria (SRE): I'll push the gateway mapping PR and cut a hotfix branch. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/gateway/pulls/1891 (draft). Hotfix adds: ```
if (quotaCall.timedOut || quotaCall.err.isDependency) {
  return clientResponse(429, {error: 'rate_limit.degraded'});
}
```

Kevin (Platform): monitoring shows 429s increased briefly as we shifted routing back to v1 (expected) and 5xx dropped to baseline. I'll let canary remain at 0% until Maria's PR is in prod.

Elliot (Customer): appreciate the fast response. Please let me know when it's safe to ramp.

Jessica (Support): ETA for hotfix to prod? Maria?

Maria (SRE): cut branch + tests in ~30m, staging deploy in 1h, prod hotfix ~2-3h if no blockers. I'll update thread when merged and deployed.

Tyler (API): action items recap: 
- Kevin: confirm canary rollback completed and keep canary=0 until further notice. (done)
- Maria: PR + hotfix mapping to 429, run staging tests.
- Jessica: notify affected customers, offer credits if they show production impact.
- Anita: stand by for billing cases.
- Tyler: follow up on quota-service scaling ticket INFRA-3245.

SRE Bot: incident status: mitigated (canary rollback) at 2026-03-01T10:28:00Z. Monitoring window open for 60m.

Maria (SRE): postmortem notes for later: misroute + insufficient failure-mapping in gateway + quota-service dependency scaling. Recommend: validate canary health checks include dependency call latencies, and enforce mapping of quota failures to 4xx.

Jessica (Support): closing customer loop: Elliot we'll send an incident summary and postmortem once available. Thanks for patience. :pray:

Elliot (Customer): thanks all, appreciate the quick follow-up.

Tyler (API): updating ticket INFRA-3245 with rollback timeline and mitigation. Will link to gateway PR when merged.

Maria (SRE): update 10:48 UTC: PR merged to main, staged, running canary tests. Rolling hotfix to prod at 10:55 UTC.

SRE Bot: deploy success: gateway hotfix v1.4.3 rolled to prod at 2026-03-01T10:55:22Z. Post-deploy 5xx returned to baseline (<0.5%).

Jessica (Support): notified customer and confirmed they no longer see 502s. Closing escalation.

Tyler (API): follow-up item: add automated test that ensures quota timeouts are translated to 429 in gateway e2e tests. Created ticket GATEWAY-882.

Maria (SRE): will include in postmortem. Closing thread after postmortem published.

Jessica (Support): thread closing. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
